coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED. (1) Wikipedia "1995 Nebraska Cornhuskers football team" — infobox plus the "Roster and coaching staff" navbox, which lists Osborne + 9 on-field assistants + Boyd Epley only. (2) PRIMARY SOURCE, and by far the richest: the official "Nebraska Football 1995 Media Guide" (preseason-1995 guide for the championship season), full OCR text on archive.org at https://archive.org/download/nebraska-football-1995-media-guide-b/Nebraska%20Football%2C%201995%20Media%20Guide%20%28B%29_djvu.txt — its "1995 Quick Facts" directory names the coaching staff, athletic medicine staff and support staff by exact title, and its bio pages cover the two graduate assistants, the whole Athletic Performance (S&C) unit, football operations, equipment, video and football-office staff. (3) The Oct. 21, 1995 Nebraska vs. Kansas State game program, full OCR text at https://archive.org/download/1995-10-21-kansas-state-at-nebraska-football-game-program-c/1995-10-21%2C%20Kansas%20State%20at%20Nebraska%20Football%20Game%20Program%20%28C%29_djvu.txt — contains an in-season "Husker Football Coaching Staff" photo page (confirming both GAs were still on staff in-season), a full "University of Nebraska Athletic Staff" photo directory, and dedicated photo pages for the undergraduate assistant coaches, equipment managers and video crew. I did not need the Wayback Machine; huskers.com did not exist in 1995.

WHAT IS FULLY RECOVERED. Head coach; all 9 on-field assistants (Solich, McBride, Bohl, Brown, Darlington, Gill, Samuel, Tenopir, Young) — this is the complete on-field staff, NCAA rules of the era capped it at 9 assistants; both graduate assistant football coaches (Carlin, Grant); the complete 7-person Athletic Performance/S&C staff; football operations and the three football-office secretaries; the athletic medicine staff and team physicians; equipment; video; the six undergraduate assistant coaches; academic services.

WHAT I COULD NOT RECOVER / CAVEATS. (a) There is no "analyst" or "quality control" tier in 1995 — those job categories did not exist in college football then. The closest analogues are the two GAs and the six undergraduate assistant coaches, which I have listed. No row is categorized qc or analyst because no source uses those words. (b) UNIT SCOPE: Nebraska in 1995 ran Athletic Performance, Athletic Medicine, Video, Equipment and Academic Services as DEPARTMENT-WIDE units serving all 22 sports rather than as football-only staffs. I included the members documented in the football media guide, and I have flagged in each person's source note where the guide explicitly assigns that person to a non-football sport (Paul Koch = basketball/Olympic sports; Cindy Barker = women's basketball; Sara Weinberg = track and field). A consumer wanting a strictly football-only roster should drop those three. I deliberately EXCLUDED athletics-department administrators with no documented football role (AD Bill Byrne, Bob Devaney, Al Papik, Don Bryant, Barbara Hibner, Gary Fouraker, Joe Selig, ticket/grounds/marketing/compliance/development, and the sports information staff). (c) NOT ENUMERATED AS ROWS, though documented in the sources and available if wanted: the five graduate assistant TRAINERS for 1995-96 (Doug Edwards, Tara Kramer, Ben Vance, Carol Young, Chris Froiland) and ~19 student trainers, both named in the Jerry Weber bio in the media guide; and the 13 student football managers named in the game program ("1995 Husker Student Managers, Back Row (from left): Jon Meier, Adam Kucera, Ryan Ricenbae, Mike Schukei, John McNeely, Jason Joseph, Jason"). These are student/GA labor rather than staff, so I left them out of the rows rather than pad the count — but they are real and sourced. (d) TITLE CONFLICTS between the two 1995 sources, left as-is rather than silently resolved: Randy Gobel is "Assistant Director of Athletic Performance" in the media guide but "Coordinator of Strength & Conditioning" in the program's photo directory; George Sullivan is "Head Trainer Emeritus" in the media guide but the program's photo directory still captions him "Asst. Chief of Staff, Head Football Trainer" (the program directory appears partly stale — the media guide states he retired as full-time football trainer after 1994 and stayed on as a consultant, and the program elsewhere notes a Sept. 22, 1995 retirement reception for him). (e) OCR CAVEAT: both archive.org sources are OCR'd scans. Every quote below is copied byte-exact from the OCR text, so a few contain OCR artifacts (e.g. "Fat Logsdon" for Pat Logsdon, "Bryan Balley" for Bryan Bailey, "Faul Koch" for Paul Koch, "isin"/"yearas" run-together words, curly apostrophes). I chose quote lines that are clean where possible and used the `note` field to carry role context that falls on an adjacent OCR line. Photo-caption directories in the program place names on one line and titles on the following lines in column order; where I relied on that, the note explains the column mapping. (f) No mid-season arrivals or departures are documented for any staff member; the entire staff listed was in place for the Jan. 2, 1996 Fiesta Bowl. Craig Bohl was in his first season as LB coach (replacing Kevin Steele, who left for the NFL after 1994) but was hired before the season, not mid-season.
